page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-24 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores, supporting 2 threads per core at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The memory configuration consists of 90.0 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for vector and matrix operations.

Benchmark results position this instance in the average tier for most compute and memory tasks, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1912.0 and a multi-core score of 13690.0. It demonstrates strong performance in image processing and text processing, both placing in the top 25% of tested systems. For language model workloads, the instance achieves top-tier performance in text generation for small 135M models at 396.71 tokens per second, though performance scales down to 17.23 tokens per second for medium 7B models. Memory bandwidth reaches 139.38 GB/sec for large uncached read blocks and 58.03 GB/sec for write operations.

This instance does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached options. It also lacks complimentary public IPv4 addresses. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-standard-24 offers a balanced resource density for workloads requiring dedicated x86_64 CPU resources without the premium cost of GPU-accelerated or memory-optimized hardware. It is suitable for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference.
